h1: Dheva Resort Chachoengsao — a small riverside resort on the Bang Pakong where you actually slow down
intro: If you want to escape the city and sleep beside the Bang Pakong river, with nothing but the sound of water and wind across the rice fields — Dheva Resort is a small place in Khlong Khuean that keeps coming up. It's a 16-room boutique resort in a country-farm style, right on the river, with rooms whose balconies look out over the water and the paddies. The draws are the privacy, the owner's homemade cooking, and the farm-style activities like riding the e-taek cart through the orchards and herbal foot soaks. Rates start at about ฿1,500/night for the room only, or you can take a package with several meals included from around ฿3,200. The trade-off is the location, well out of town — you'll need your own car.

body.html: What sets Dheva Resort apart from the in-town hotels in Chachoengsao is its small size and sense of privacy. The whole resort has just 16 rooms, spread across a riverside plot on the Bang Pakong in Khlong Khuean district. The rooms are country-farm in style, all warm wood and earth tones, and many have a balcony where you can watch the river or the rice fields in the morning. Most guests come specifically to rest quietly rather than for anything flashy — and that's exactly the calm they get.

The thing real reviews mention most is the food and the owner's hospitality. The kitchen serves homemade Thai dishes and house-made desserts, with an afternoon tea sitting by the water. Several guests say it feels more like visiting relatives who happen to cook beautifully than checking into a hotel. The owner and staff look after you personally — the kind of charm a small resort can offer that a big hotel can't.

Beyond lounging by the river, there are farm activities and a slow-life rhythm to enjoy. You can ride the e-taek farm cart around the orchards and paddies, soak your feet in herbal water, and stroll along the riverside. It suits families wanting to give the kids a taste of nature, as well as couples after a quiet, photogenic spot. The sunset over the Bang Pakong in the evening is the moment most guests love best.
"A small resort but so warm — the owner is lovely, the homemade food was delicious every meal, and you can sit on the balcony watching the river all day. We came back genuinely rested."

To be straight with you, Dheva Resort is a small place with not many online reviews. Its scores on the booking platforms are very high, but they come from a small number of reviewers, because it's a niche stay better known through word of mouth among Thai travellers than to general tourists. If you like the certainty of a chain hotel with thousands of reviews, this will feel different — it's a boutique homestay-style stay that lives or dies on the owner's care.

The thing to plan around is that it's far from town and you need a car. Khlong Khuean is rural riverside country, a fair drive from central Chachoengsao and Wat Sothon. There are no convenience stores or restaurants within walking distance, so you'll rely on the resort's kitchen or bring your own supplies. Anyone arriving by public transport without onward wheels will struggle — far better to drive yourself or hire a car.

Overall, Dheva Resort is for travellers who want to escape the noise, sleep by the river at a slow pace, eat good homemade food and have some privacy. Rates start around ฿1,500 for the room only, with full-board packages (breakfast, snack and dinner) from about ฿3,200 for those who want every meal handled. If you can accept the out-of-town location and the small, homestay scale, it delivers a Bang Pakong riverside atmosphere that's hard to find in ordinary hotels.

tips.title: Take a meal-inclusive package
tips.body: The homemade food is the highlight here — if you're staying over, choose a package with breakfast, snack and dinner included, since there's nowhere to walk to nearby.

tips.title: Driving is by far easiest
tips.body: Khlong Khuean is rural riverside country, well out of town — driving yourself or hiring a car is the most practical option. Allow a fair drive of several tens of minutes.

tips.title: Don't miss the riverside sunset
tips.body: The sunset over the Bang Pakong is the prettiest moment of the day — book a room with a river-facing balcony and sip the afternoon tea while you wait for it.

tips.title: Book and ask ahead
tips.body: With only 16 rooms, it fills fast on holidays — call to book and ask about the activities (e-taek cart, herbal foot soak) with the resort in advance.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Dheva Resort Chachoengsao

faq.q: Where is Dheva Resort in Chachoengsao, and how do you get there?
faq.a: Dheva Resort is at 78 Moo 3, Khlong Khuean Subdistrict, Khlong Khuean District, Chachoengsao, on the Bang Pakong river. It's rural riverside country, around 30 minutes by car from town and Wat Sothon. Driving yourself or hiring a car is recommended, as there's no public transport or shops within walking distance.

faq.q: How much does Dheva Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿1,500/night for the room only. There are Deluxe and Grand Deluxe rooms, plus full-board packages including breakfast, snack and dinner from around ฿3,200–4,200 for those who want every meal handled. Compare a few platforms and ask the resort about packages before booking.

faq.q: What activities does Dheva Resort offer?
faq.a: It focuses on the riverside setting and farm activities. You can ride the e-taek cart around the orchards and paddies, soak your feet in herbal water, and relax by the Bang Pakong river, with a fine sunset over the water in the evening. It suits both families introducing kids to nature and couples wanting somewhere quiet.

faq.q: What are the rooms and food like at Dheva Resort?
faq.a: Rooms are country-farm in style, with wood and earth tones, and many have a balcony facing the river or rice fields. The thing real reviews praise most is the owner's homemade food and house-made desserts, plus a riverside afternoon tea. The welcome is warm in the way only a small resort can be.

faq.q: Who is Dheva Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for travellers who want to escape the city and sleep slowly by the river, eat good homemade food and enjoy privacy. Because it's a small 16-room resort in rural riverside country, it's less suited to those who want full big-hotel facilities, or to anyone without their own car.

faq.q: Can you bring pets to Dheva Resort?
faq.a: Yes. The resort allows pets for an extra fee, and you should give advance notice when booking. As a small resort with riverside grounds and a garden, it's a good fit for bringing your dog or cat along — but confirm the conditions with the resort directly.
